assessments.reasoning: The Index's own decision at commit d305c6ff9c1711877265b61cf44bfc1e0c09370b is primary evidence for its editorial assignment. The complete 1,997-byte capture includes the row binding 1a07620194554b8db89bfcbfc70c3e05, lppl-1-3c-publisher-reference and the claimed publisher digest to LPPL-1.3c. The other rows have distinct identifiers and digests. The closing reference to separate publisher wording cannot establish that SPDX omits the passage.

The complete 700-byte GitHub API record from spdx/license-list-data identifies annotated tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b. Its tag field is v3.29.0 and its target type is commit. The target SHA matches the detail record's revision exactly. The tagger date is 2026-09-16, before the cutoff. GitHub reports the tag as unsigned, so attribution rests on the repository record without signature assurance.

The project-hosted plaintext at https://www.latex-project.org/lppl/lppl-1-3c.txt names the LaTeX3 Project. Two contiguous partitions cover all 19,036 bytes and report SHA-256 c1ae6e179a6d28bbd5c483fbacc744acc75e922d598281dc3390aab26126e163, matching the Index row. Part 1 supplies the edition and header date. Part 2 supplies the publisher example and the nonreplacement passage. The example's distribution year serves a different purpose from the edition header date.

The SPDX repository's json/details/LPPL-1.3c.json at the tagged commit is primary evidence for the listing. Six contiguous partitions cover all 84,386 bytes and report SHA-256 6094d0c52c12dcf3fa5d5aede2e59968fe6bc91cd0edd308db4df4553829298d. Part 1 gives the dated licenseText header and isDeprecatedLicenseId false. Part 2 contains the differing example and the shared nonreplacement passage. Part 3 gives the identifier, edition name and release comment of 4 May 2008. Its seeAlso entries are http://www.latex-project.org/lppl/LPPL-1.3c.txt and https://opensource.org/license/LPPL-1.3c. The first differs from the capture URL in scheme, filename case and version punctuation. The second names an OSI page.

limitations: The finding concerns a lexical discovery association. Legal equivalence, redistribution rights, work-specific grants and installation remain outside its scope.

The SPDX tag and detail record share one repository lineage. SPDX is the original authority for its listing, and the LaTeX Project is the original authority for its plaintext. Repeated text in SPDX templates and HTML supplies no independent corroboration.
The frozen records establish what the two seeAlso entries say. Whether either URL resolves to the captured plaintext remains unverified.

This is a research finding under SCES-1.0. The Index decision leaves discovery dispositions unresolved pending protected integration. Independent review and publication qualification are separate decisions.
reasoning: The Index decision assigns LPPL-1.3c to the exact digest of the inspected LaTeX Project plaintext. The SPDX tag v3.29.0 points to commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, whose license detail record gives licenseId LPPL-1.3c and names LaTeX Project Public License v1.3c. The publisher header and SPDX licenseText both identify LPPL Version 1.3c and give the date 2008-05-04. These records establish the claimed documentary correspondence at the 2026-11-27 America/Chicago cutoff.
